n%20%E2%80%94%20it%20already%20runs.%20The%20goal%20is%20to%20connect%20three%20things%3A%20the%20equations%20of%20the%20model%2C%20the%20step-by-step%20numerical%20integration%2C%20and%20the%20muscle%20behavior%20you%20see%20in%20the%20plots.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Before%20you%20begin%2C%20picture%20an%20*isometric*%20contraction%3A%20the%20whole%20muscle%E2%80%93tendon%20unit%20is%20held%20at%20a%20fixed%20length%20while%20the%20muscle%20activates.%20Predict%20what%20happens%20to%20the%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20%24L_M%24%20and%20to%20the%20tendon%20length%20%24L_T%24%20as%20activation%20rises.%20Can%20either%20one%20change%20even%20though%20their%20sum%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%24%20is%20fixed%3F%20Write%20your%20answer%20down%3B%20you%20will%20test%20it%20in%20the%20first%20simulation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Follow%20the%20existing%20pennation%20and%20equilibrium%20examples%20into%20the%20isometric%20and%20prescribed-length%20simulations.%20The%20total%20musculotendon%20length%20is%20an%20input%20here%3B%20fiber%20length%20is%20a%20state.%20Check%20force%20balance%20and%20step-size%20sensitivity%20before%20interpreting%20differences%20between%20parameter%20choices.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Try%20the%20distributed%20**Exercises**%20before%20opening%20their%20collapsed%20worked%20solutions.%20Then%20use%20the%20**Checkpoint%20questions**%20and%20attempt%20the%20**Problems**%20independently%3B%20their%20panels%20contain%20final%20answers%20only.%20Predict%20the%20effect%20of%20a%20parameter%20change%20before%20running%20it%2C%20and%20check%20units%20and%20limiting%20cases.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Opening%20challenge.**%20Clamp%20the%20total%20musculotendon%20length%20and%20increase%20excitation.%20Can%20the%20muscle%20fibers%20still%20shorten%2C%20and%20where%20would%20that%20shortening%20go%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20% %0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20L_M%20%3D%20L_%7BCE%7D%20%3D%20L_%7BPE%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdot%7BL%7D_M%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7BL%7D_%7BCE%7D%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7BL%7D_%7BPE%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7BM%7D%20%3D%20F_%7BCE%7D%20%2B%20F_%7BPE%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20If%20we%20assume%20that%20the%20muscle%E2%80%93tendon%20system%20is%20at%20equilibrium%2C%20that%20is%2C%20muscle%2C%20%24F_%7BM%7D%24%2C%20and%20tendon%2C%20%24F_%7BT%7D%24%2C%20forces%20are%20in%20equilibrium%20at%20all%20times%2C%20the%20following%20equation%20holds%20(and%20that%20a%20muscle%20can%20only%20pull)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7BT%7D%20%3D%20F_%7BSE%7D%20%3D%20F_%7BM%7D%5Ccos%5Calpha%0A%20%20%20%20%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%201.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20In%20the%20relationship%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%20%3D%20L_T%20%2B%20L_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%24%2C%20which%20lengths%20change%20over%20the%20course%20of%20a%20simulation%2C%20and%20which%20one%20do%20*we*%20prescribe%20as%20an%20input%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20equilibrium%20assumption%20sets%20%24F_T%20%3D%20F_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%24%20at%20every%20instant.%20What%20property%20of%20the%20tendon%20makes%20treating%20it%20as%20always%20in%20equilibrium%20with%20the%20muscle%20a%20reasonable%20simplification%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20If%20the%20tendon%20stretches%20while%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%24%20is%20held%20fixed%2C%20what%20must%20happen%20to%20the%20fiber%20length%20%24L_M%24%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Pennation%20angle%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20pennation%20angle%20will%20vary%20during%20muscle%20activation%3B%20for%20instance%2C%20Kawakami%20et%20al.%20(1998)%20showed%20that%20the%20pennation%20angle%20of%20the%20medial%20gastrocnemius%20muscle%20can%20vary%20from%2022%24%5Eo%24%20to%2067%24%5Eo%24%20during%20activation.%20The%20most%20used%20approach%20is%20to%20assume%20that%20the%20muscle%20width%20(defined%20as%20the%20length%20of%20the%20perpendicular%20line%20between%20the%20lines%20of%20the%20muscle%20origin%20and%20insertion)%20remains%20constant%20(Scott%20%26%20Winter%2C%201991)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20w%20%3D%20L_%7BM%2C0%7D%20%5Csin%5Calpha_0%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20pennation%20angle%20as%20a%20function%20of%20time%20will%20be%20given%20by%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Calpha%20%3D%20%5Csin%5E%7B-1%7D%20%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7Bw%7D%7BL_M%7D%5Cright)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20cosine%20of%20the%20pennation%20angle%20can%20be%20given%20by%20(if%20%24L_M%24%20is%20known)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ccos%20%5Calpha%20%3D%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Csqrt%7BL_M%5E2-w%5E2%7D%7D%7BL_M%7D%20%3D%20%5Csqrt%7B1-%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7Bw%7D%7BL_M%7D%5Cright)%5E2%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20or%20(if%20%24L_M%24%20is%20not%20known)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ccos%20%5Calpha%20%3D%20%5Cdfrac%7BL_%7BMT%7D-L_T%7D%7BL_M%7D%20%3D%20%5Cdfrac%7B1%7D%7B%5Csqrt%7B1%20%2B%20%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7Bw%7D%7BL_%7BMT%7D-L_T%7D%5Cright)%5E2%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%202.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20tendon%20feels%20the%20force%20%24F_T%20%3D%20F_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%24.%20As%20the%20pennation%20angle%20%24%5Calpha%24%20grows%20during%20a%20contraction%2C%20does%20the%20tendon%20receive%20a%20larger%20or%20smaller%20fraction%20of%20the%20muscle%20fiber%20force%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20constant-width%20assumption%20(%24w%20%3D%20L_%7BM%2C0%7D%5Csin%5Calpha_0%24)%20forces%20%24%5Calpha%24%20to%20change%20as%20the%20fiber%20shortens.%20Using%20%24%5Calpha%20%3D%20%5Csin%5E%7B-1%7D(w%2FL_M)%24%2C%20explain%20whether%20the%20angle%20grows%20or%20shrinks%20when%20%24L_M%24%20decreases.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%201.**%20A%20fusiform%20muscle%20has%20%24%5Calpha_0%20%3D%200%24.%20Show%20from%20%24w%20%3D%20L_%7BM%2C0%7D%5Csin%5Calpha_0%24%20that%20its%20width%20%24w%24%20is%20zero%2C%20so%20%24%5Calpha%20%3D%200%24%20and%20%24%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%3D%201%24%20for%20any%20fiber%20length.%20We%20will%20use%20%24%5Calpha_0%20%3D%200%24%20for%20most%20simulations%20and%20revisit%20a%20pennated%20(%2430%5Eo%24)%20case%20later.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%201%20%E2%80%94%20Project%20fiber%20length.**%20A%20fiber%20is%200.10%20m%20long%20at%2030%C2%B0%20pennation.%20Find%20its%20projection%20along%20the%20tendon.%20If%20fiber%20height%20is%20constant%2C%20what%20happens%20to%20pennation%20as%20fiber%20length%20decreases%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Solution%20to%20Exercise%201'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20projection%20is%20%24L_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%3D0.0866%24%20m.%20Constant%20height%20means%20%24L_M%5Csin%5Calpha%24%20is%20fixed%2C%20so%20shortening%20increases%20%24%5Calpha%24.%20The%20geometry%20must%20be%20updated%20during%20a%20simulation.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Muscle%20force%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20general%2C%20the%20dependence%20of%20the%20force%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20with%20its%20length%20and%20velocity%20and%20with%20the%20activation%20level%20are%20assumed%20independent%20of%20each%20other%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7BCE%7D(a%2C%20L_%7BCE%7D%2C%20%5Cdot%7BL%7D_%7BCE%7D)%20%3D%20a%20%5C%3A%20f_l(L_%7BCE%7D)%20%5C%3A%20f_v(%5Cdot%7BL%7D_%7BCE%7D)%20%5C%3A%20F_%7BM0%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24f_l(L_M)%24%20and%20%24f_v(%5Cdot%7BL%7D_M)%24%20are%20mathematical%20functions%20describing%20the%20force-length%20and%20force-velocity%20relationships%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20(typically%20these%20functions%20are%20normalized%20by%20%24F_%7BM0%7D%24%2C%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20(at%20zero%20velocity)%20muscle%20force%2C%20so%20we%20have%20to%20multiply%20the%20right%20side%20of%20the%20equation%20by%20%24F_%7BM0%7D%24).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20And%20for%20the%20muscle%20force%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7BM%7D(a%2C%20L_M%2C%20%5Cdot%7BL%7D_M)%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5Ba%20%5C%3A%20f_l(L_M)f_v(%5Cdot%7BL%7D_M)%20%2B%20F_%7BPE%7D(L_M)%5Cright%5DF_%7BM0%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20This%20equation%20for%20the%20muscle%20force%2C%20with%20%24a%24%2C%20%24L_%7BM%7D%24%2C%20and%20%24%5Cdot%7BL%7D_%7BM%7D%24%20as%20state%20variables%2C%20can%20be%20used%20to%20simulate%20the%20dynamics%20of%20a%20muscle%20given%20an%20excitation%20and%20determine%20the%20muscle%20force%20and%20length.%20We%20can%20rearrange%20the%20equation%2C%20invert%20the%20expression%20for%20%24f_v%24%2C%20and%20integrate%20the%20resulting%20first-order%20ordinary%20differential%20equation%20(ODE)%20to%20obatin%20%24L_M%24%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdot%7BL%7D_M%20%3D%20f_v%5E%7B-1%7D%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7BF_%7BSE%7D(L_%7BMT%7D-L_M%5Ccos%5Calpha)%2F%5Ccos%5Calpha%20-%20F_%7BPE%7D(L_M)%7D%7Ba%20f_l(L_M)%7D%5Cright)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20This%20approach%20is%20the%20most%20commonly%20employed%20in%20the%20literature%20(see%20for%20example%2C%20%5BOpenSim%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fsimtk-confluence.stanford.edu%3A8080%2Fdisplay%2FOpenSim%2FMuscle%2BModel%2BTheory%2Band%2BPublications)%3B%20McLean%2C%20Su%2C%20van%20den%20Bogert%2C%202003%3B%20Thelen%2C%202003%3B%20Nigg%20and%20Herzog%2C%202007).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Although%20the%20equation%20for%20the%20muscle%20force%20doesn't%20have%20numerical%20singularities%2C%20the%20differential%20equation%20for%20muscle%20velocity%20has%20four%20(%5BOpenSim%20Millard%202012%20Muscle%20Models%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fsimtk-confluence.stanford.edu%3A8080%2Fdisplay%2FOpenSim%2FMillard%2B2012%2BMuscle%2BModels))%3A%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20When%20%24a%20%5Crightarrow%200%24%3B%20when%20%24f_l(L_M)%20%5Crightarrow%200%24%3B%20when%20%24%5Calpha%20%5Crightarrow%20%5Cpi%2F2%24%3B%20and%20when%20%24%5Cpartial%20f_v%2F%5Cpartial%20v%20%5Crightarrow%200%24.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20The%20following%20solutions%20can%20be%20employed%20to%20avoid%20the%20numerical%20singularities%20(%5BOpenSim%20Millard%202012%20Muscle%20Models%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fsimtk-confluence.stanford.edu%3A8080%2Fdisplay%2FOpenSim%2FMillard%2B2012%2BMuscle%2BModels))%3A%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20-%20A%20minimum%20value%20for%20%24a%24%3B%20e.g.%2C%20%24a_%7Bmin%7D%3D0.01%24%3B%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20-%20A%20minimum%20value%20for%20%24f_l(L_M)%24%3B%20e.g.%2C%20%24f_l(0.1)%24%3B%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20-%20A%20maximum%20value%20for%20pennation%20angle%3B%20e.g.%2C%20constrain%20%24%5Calpha%24%20to%20%24%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%3E%200.1%3B%20(%5Calpha%20%3C%2084.26%5Eo)%24%3B%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20-%20Make%20the%20slope%20of%20%24f_V%24%20at%20and%20beyond%20maximum%20velocity%20different%20than%20zero%20(for%20both%20concentric%20and%20eccentric%20activations).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20will%20adopt%20these%20solutions%20to%20avoid%20singularities%20in%20the%20simulation%20of%20muscle%20mechanics.%20A%20problem%20of%20imposing%20values%20to%20variables%20as%20described%20above%20is%20that%20we%20can%20make%20the%20ordinary%20differential%20equation%20numerically%20stiff%2C%20which%20will%20increase%20the%20computational%20cost%20of%20the%20numerical%20integration.%20A%20better%20solution%20would%20be%20to%20modify%20the%20model%20to%20not%20have%20these%20singularities%20(see%20%5BOpenSim%20Millard%202012%20Muscle%20Models%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fsimtk-confluence.stanford.edu%3A8080%2Fdisplay%2FOpenSim%2FMillard%2B2012%2BMuscle%2BModels)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%203.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20muscle%20force%20%24F_%7BM%7D%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5Ba%20%5C%3A%20f_l(L_M)f_v(%5Cdot%7BL%7D_M)%20%2B%20F_%7BPE%7D(L_M)%5Cright%5DF_%7BM0%7D%24%20has%20three%20factors%20that%20scale%20the%20*active*%20force.%20Which%20factor%20carries%20the%20neural%20command%2C%20which%20the%20length%20dependence%2C%20and%20which%20the%20velocity%20dependence%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20velocity%20equation%20is%20obtained%20by%20inverting%20%24f_v%24%2C%20which%20divides%20by%20%24a%5C%2Cf_l(L_M)%24.%20Why%20does%20this%20create%20a%20numerical%20singularity%20when%20the%20muscle%20is%20nearly%20inactive%20(%24a%5Cto%200%24)%20or%20far%20from%20its%20optimal%20length%20(%24f_l%5Cto%200%24)%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%202.**%20For%20each%20of%20the%20four%20singularities%20listed%20above%20(%24a%5Cto%200%24%2C%20%24f_l%5Cto%200%24%2C%20%24%5Calpha%5Cto%5Cpi%2F2%24%2C%20%24%5Cpartial%20f_v%2F%5Cpartial%20v%5Cto%200%24)%2C%20find%20the%20matching%20clamp%20in%20the%20code%20when%20you%20reach%20the%20module%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%20notebook.%20(Hint%3A%20look%20for%20%600.1%20*%20lmopt%60%20in%20%60vm_eq%60%20and%20the%20pennation-angle%20cap%20in%20%60penn_ang%60.)%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%202%20%E2%80%94%20Separate%20active%20and%20tendon%20forces.**%20A%20fiber%20has%20300%20N%20active%20and%20100%20N%20passive%20force%20at%2020%C2%B0%20pennation.%20What%20tendon%20force%20is%20consistent%20with%20equilibrium%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Solution%20to%20Exercise%202'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Total%20fiber%20force%20is%20400%20N%3B%20its%20tendon-direction%20component%20is%20%24400%5Ccos20%5E%5Ccirc%3D375.9%24%20N.%20Equating%20tendon%20force%20to%20active%20force%20alone%20would%20neglect%20both%20passive%20tension%20and%20pennation.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Simulation%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20simulate%20muscle%20dynamics%20using%20the%20Thelen2003Muscle%20model%20we%20defined%20in%20%5BMuscle%20modeling%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_modeling.py).%20For%20the%20simulation%20of%20the%20Thelen2003Muscle%2C%20we%20simply%20have%20to%20integrate%20the%20equation%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20V_M%20%3D%20(0.25%2B0.75a)%5C%2CV_%7BMmax%7D%5Cfrac%7B%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M-a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%7D%7Bb%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20b%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5C%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%2B%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M%2FA_f%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M%20%5Cleq%20a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(shortening)%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cdfrac%7B(2%2B2%2FA_f)(a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BCEmax%7D%20-%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M)%7D%7B%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BCEmax%7D-1%7D%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M%20%3E%20a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(lengthening)%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%5Cright.%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20equation%20above%20already%20contains%20the%20terms%20for%20actvation%2C%20%24a%24%2C%20and%20force-length%20dependence%2C%20%24%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%24.%20The%20equation%20is%20too%20complicated%20for%20solving%20analytically%2C%20we%20will%20solve%20it%20by%20numerical%20integration%20with%20a%20simple%20fixed-step%20forward%20%5BEuler%20method%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FEuler_method).%20We%20could%20run%20a%20simulation%20using%20%5BOpenSim%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fsimtk.org%2Fhome%2Fopensim)%3B%20it%20would%20be%20faster%2C%20but%20for%20fun%2C%20let's%20program%20in%20Python.%20All%20the%20necessary%20functions%20for%20the%20Thelen2003Muscle%20model%20described%20in%20%5BMuscle%20modeling%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_modeling.py)%20were%20grouped%20in%20one%20file%20(module)%2C%20%60muscles.py%60.%20Besides%20these%20functions%2C%20the%20module%20%60muscles.py%60%20contains%20a%20function%20for%20the%20muscle%20velocity%2C%20%60vm_eq%60%2C%20which%20is%20evaluated%20at%20each%20integration%20step%20by%20the%20solver%20%60lm_sol%60%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60python%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20def%20vm_eq(self%2C%20t%2C%20lm%2C%20lm0%2C%20lmt0%2C%20lmopt%2C%20ltslack%2C%20alpha0%2C%20vmmax%2C%20fm0)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22%5C%22%5C%22Equation%20for%20muscle%20velocity.%22%5C%22%5C%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20if%20lm%20%3C%200.1*lmopt%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20lm%20%3D%200.1*lmopt%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a%20%20%20%20%20%3D%20self.activation(t)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20lmt%20%20%20%3D%20self.lmt_eq(t%2C%20lmt0)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20alpha%20%3D%20self.penn_ang(lmt%3Dlmt%2C%20lm%3Dlm%2C%20lm0%3Dlm0%2C%20alpha0%3Dalpha0)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20lt%20%20%20%20%3D%20lmt%20-%20lm*np.cos(alpha)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fse%20%20%20%3D%20self.force_se(lt%3Dlt%2C%20ltslack%3Dltslack)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fpe%20%20%20%3D%20self.force_pe(lm%3Dlm%2Flmopt)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fl%20%20%20%20%3D%20self.force_l(lm%3Dlm%2Flmopt)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fce_t%20%3D%20fse%2Fnp.cos(alpha)%20-%20fpe%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20vm%20%20%20%20%3D%20self.velo_fm(fm%3Dfce_t%2C%20a%3Da%2C%20fl%3Dfl)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20vm%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20lm_sol(self%2C%20fun%2C%20t0%2C%20t1%2C%20dt%2C%20lm0%2C%20lmt0%2C%20ltslack%2C%20lmopt%2C%20al D%201%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20lim%20%3D%20%5Bnp.nanmin(x)%20-%20rang%20*%20margin%2C%20np.nanmax(x)%20%2B%20rang%20*%20margin%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20lim%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(Thelen2003%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20marimo%20as%20mo%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(mo%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Checkpoint%20questions%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Pause%20here%20and%20answer%20these%20before%20moving%20on.%20They%20tie%20together%20the%20pieces%20you%20have%20simulated.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20In%20a%20fixed-length%20(isometric)%20muscle%E2%80%93tendon%20unit%2C%20why%20can%20the%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20still%20change%20after%20activation%20changes%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Which%20two%20force%E2%80%93length%20curves%20add%20together%20to%20give%20the%20total%20muscle%20force%2C%20and%20which%20one%20dominates%20at%20long%20fiber%20lengths%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20does%20the%20tendon%20force%20equal%20%24F_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%24%20rather%20than%20%24F_M%24%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Activation%20lags%20behind%20excitation.%20Which%20state%20variable%20stores%20this%20%22memory%22%2C%20and%20which%20two%20parameters%20set%20how%20fast%20it%20rises%20and%20falls%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20The%20solver%20clamps%20the%20fiber%20length%20at%20%240.1%5C%2CL_%7BM%2Copt%7D%24%20and%20the%20pennation%20angle%20below%20%24%5Csim%2084%5Eo%24.%20What%20numerical%20problem%20is%20each%20clamp%20preventing%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20When%20would%20a%20coarse%20forward-Euler%20solution%20be%20good%20enough%20for%20teaching%2C%20and%20when%20would%20you%20switch%20to%20an%20adaptive%20solver%20such%20as%20%60solve_ivp%60%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Checkpoint%20answers'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Tendon%20stretch%20and%20changing%20pennation%20allow%20fiber%20shortening%20at%20fixed%20total%20length.%202.%20Active%20and%20passive%20fiber%20curves%20add%3B%20the%20passive%20curve%20dominates%20sufficiently%20long%20lengths.%203.%20Only%20the%20fiber-force%20component%20along%20the%20tendon%20is%20transmitted%20in%20this%20geometry.%204.%20Activation%20a%20stores%20the%20history%3B%20%60t_act%60%20and%20%60t_deact%60%20set%20its%20rise%2Fdecay%20rates.%205.%20The%20length%20floor%20avoids%20extreme%2Fundefined%20force%E2%80%93velocity%20calculations%3B%20the%20angle%20limit%20avoids%20division%20by%20nearly%20zero%20cosine.%20These%20safeguards%20do%20not%20validate%20impossible%20geometry.%206.%20Euler%20is%20useful%20for%20a%20converged%20short%20teaching%20demonstration%3B%20use%20an%20adaptive%20solver%20for%20fast%20transients%2C%20tighter%20accuracy%20or%20sensitive%20comparisons.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Use%20these%20as%20independent%20investigations.%20State%20the%20parameter%20choices%20and%20numerical%20tolerances%20with%20each%20result.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20**Activation%20level.**%20Run%20the%20activation%20dynamics%20with%20a%20constant%20excitation%20of%20%24u%3D1%24%2C%20%24u%3D0.5%24%2C%20and%20%24u%3D0.1%24.%20How%20does%20the%20steady-state%20muscle%20force%20scale%20with%20activation%3F%20Is%20it%20linear%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20**Tendon%20compliance.**%20Change%20the%20tendon%20slack%20length%20%60ltslack%60%20and%2For%20%60epst0%60%20to%20make%20the%20tendon%20stiffer%2C%20then%20softer.%20In%20the%20isometric%20contraction%2C%20how%20does%20tendon%20compliance%20change%20how%20much%20the%20muscle%20fiber%20shortens%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20**Optimal%20length.**%20Set%20the%20initial%20fiber%20length%20%60lm0%60%20below%2C%20at%2C%20and%20above%20the%20optimal%20length%20%60lmopt%60.%20Predict%20from%20the%20force%E2%80%93length%20curve%20where%20the%20active%20force%20is%20largest%2C%20then%20confirm%20with%20%60muscle_plot%60.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20**Pennation%20sweep.**%20Sweep%20%60alpha0%60%20over%20%240%5Eo%24%2C%20%2415%5Eo%24%2C%20%2430%5Eo%24%2C%20and%20%2445%5Eo%24%20(remember%20to%20adjust%20%60lmt0%60%20as%20done%20above).%20Report%20the%20tendon%20force%20at%20each%20and%20explain%20the%20trend%20using%20%24F_T%20%3D%20F_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%24.%0A%20%20%20%205.%20**Step%20size.**%20Re-run%20a%20simulation%20with%20%60ms.lm_sol(dt%3D0.01)%60%20and%20%60ms.lm_sol(dt%3D0.0001)%60.%20Where%20do%20the%20two%20solutions%20differ%2C%20and%20where%20do%20they%20agree%3F%20What%20does%20this%20tell%20you%20about%20choosing%20a%20step%20size%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20**Force%E2%80%93velocity.**%20During%20the%20prescribed%20shortening%20ramp%2C%20read%20the%20muscle%20force%20while%20the%20fiber%20is%20shortening%20and%20compare%20it%20with%20the%20isometric%20force%20at%20the%20same%20length.%20Does%20shortening%20raise%20or%20lower%20the%20active%20force%2C%20and%20why%3F%0A%20%20%20%207.%20**Your%20own%20contraction.**%20Design%20an%20excitation%20signal%20for%20a%20movement%20you%20care%20about%20(a%20quick%20tap%2C%20a%20sustained%20hold%2C%20a%20ramp).%20Predict%20the%20force%2C%20then%20simulate%20it%20by%20replacing%20%60ms.excitation%60.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Final%20answers%20to%20original%20Problems'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Steady%20activation%20tends%20to%20the%20excitation%20level.%20Active%20force%20is%20linear%20in%20activation%20only%20at%20fixed%20normalized%20fiber%20length%20and%20velocity%3B%20the%20compliant%20equilibrium%20can%20make%20the%20total%20isometric%20response%20nonlinear.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Lower%20tendon%20strain%20parameter%20%60epst0%60%20makes%20its%20force%E2%80%93strain%20curve%20stiffer%3B%20the%20fiber%20then%20shortens%20less%20while%20the%20tendon%20stretches.%20Slack%20length%20primarily%20changes%20geometry%20and%20operating%20point%20and%20should%20not%20be%20treated%20as%20a%20pure%20stiffness%20parameter.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20The%20active%20force%E2%80%93length%20multiplier%20peaks%20at%20%60lmopt%60%3B%20passive%20force%20can%20make%20total%20force%20largest%20at%20longer%20lengths.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20At%20fixed%20fiber%20force%20and%20fixed%20current%20pennation%2C%20tendon%2Ffiber%20force%20ratios%20are%201%2C%200.9659%2C%200.8660%20and%200.7071%20at%200%C2%B0%2C%2015%C2%B0%2C%2030%C2%B0%20and%2045%C2%B0.%20A%20full%20equilibrium%20sweep%20also%20changes%20fiber%20length%20and%20therefore%20need%20not%20scale%20by%20these%20factors%20alone.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20The%200.0001%20s%20solution%20should%20resolve%20rapid%20activation%20and%20tendon%20transients%20better.%20Quantitative%20differences%20depend%20on%20the%20selected%20parameters%3B%20convergence%20of%20force%20and%20fiber-length%20histories%20is%20the%20acceptance%20criterion.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Shortening%20lowers%20active%20force%20relative%20to%20isometric%20force%20at%20the%20same%20length%20and%20activation%20in%20this%20model.%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20No%20unique%20trace%20is%20expected.%20A%20brief%20excitation%20pulse%20produces%20delayed%20activation%20and%20force%2C%20followed%20by%20decay%3B%20a%20sustained%20input%20approaches%20the%20coupled%20equilibrium%20for%20the%20imposed%20length.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Go%20deeper%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BMuscle%20modeling%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_modeling.py)%20%E2%80%94%20the%20com
